There are \(20\) marked points total, so the total number of ways to choose \(3\) of them is

\[
\binom{20}{3}=1140.
\]

A choice of \(3\) points fails to form a triangle exactly when the three points are collinear.

All \(20\) marked points lie on the boundary of the regular decagon. Since a regular decagon is a strictly convex polygon, a line can contain three boundary points only if it contains an entire side of the decagon. On each side, the marked points are exactly the two vertices and the midpoint of that side, giving one collinear triple per side.

There are \(10\) sides, so there are \(10\) degenerate triples.

Thus the number of nondegenerate triangles is

\binom{20}{3}-10=1140-10=1130.
